facts.statement: Epachthosaurus was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur belonging to the subfamily Lithostrotia.
facts.quote: Epachthosaurus (meaning "heavy lizard") was a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur, belonging to Lithostrotia, from the Late Cretaceous of Central and Northern Patagonia in South America.

facts.statement: The name Epachthosaurus means "heavy lizard".
facts.quote: Epachthosaurus (meaning "heavy lizard") was a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur, belonging to Lithostrotia, from the Late Cretaceous of Central and Northern Patagonia in South America.

facts.statement: The type species Epachthosaurus sciuttoi was described by Powell in 1990.
facts.quote: The type species, E. sciuttoi, was described by Powell in 1990.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MACN-CH 1317 consists of an incomplete posterior dorsal vertebra.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is MACN-CH 1317, which consists of an incomplete posterior dorsal vertebra.

facts.statement: A nearly complete specimen, UNPSJB-PV 920, was recovered by researchers from the Universidad Nacional de la Patagonia in Argentina.
facts.quote: A nearly complete specimen referred to Epachthosaurus, UNPSJB-PV 920, was recovered during field research conducted as part of the project Los vertebrados de la Formación Bajo Barreal, Provincia de Chubut, Patagonia, Argentina by researchers from the Laboratorio de Paleontologia de Vertebrados of the Universidad Nacional de la Patagonia.

facts.statement: Epachthosaurus was a large titanosaurian approximately 18 to 20 meters long and likely lacked bony armor like Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: Epachthosaurus es un gran titanosauriano de alrededor de 18 a 20 metros de largo y posiblemente no tenía armadura ósea como el Saltasaurus.

facts.statement: A 2004 study estimated the weight of specimen UNPSJB-PV 920 at 11,290 kilograms using a water displacement method.
facts.quote: En el estudio de 2004 T. Galarza y J. Gallegos han intentado determinar el peso de UNPSJB-PV 920. Hicieron un modelo a escala de este individuo y utilizaron el método de Robert McNeill Alexander, para determinar el volumen midiendo el desplazamiento de agua en inmersión, para llegar a un peso estimado de 11,290 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Epachthosaurus is considered the most basal titanosaurid with procoelous (concave front) caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Se caracteriza por la presencia de facetas adicionales en la articulación de las vértebras, es considerado como el titanosáurido más basal con articulaciones procoelicas en las vértebras de la cola.

facts.statement: Epachthosaurus is distinguished by unique features including hyposphene-hypantrum articulations in caudal vertebrae 1 through 14 and a pedal phalangeal formula of 2-2-3-2-0.
facts.quote: The autapomorphies that distinguish Epachthosaurus from other genera are: middle and caudal dorsal vertebrae with unique articular processes extending ventrolaterally from the hyposphene; a strongly developed intraprezygapophyseal lamina, and processes projecting laterally from the dorsal portion of the spinodiapophyseal lamina; hyposphene-hypantrum articulations in caudals 1–14; and a pedal phalangeal formula of 2-2-3-2-0.

facts.statement: Epachthosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 99.6 and 93.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 99,6 y 93,5 millones de años, en el Cenomaniense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Epachthosaurus is considered the most basal known titanosaurian with procoelous caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Epachthosaurus is considered to be the most basal titanosaurian known with procoelous caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Epachthosaurus, Argentinosaurus, and Andesaurus have been included in the family Andesauridae, characterized by containing the most basal titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Esta ha hecho que Epachthosaurus, Argentinosaurus, y Andesaurus hayan sido incluidos en una nueva familia llamada Andesauridae, caracterizado por contener a los más basales titanosaurios.

facts.statement: The exact systematic position of Epachthosaurus within Titanosauria is unclear.
facts.quote: La posición sistemática exacta dentro del Titanosauria no está clara.

facts.statement: Research suggests Epachthosaurus was a basal Titanosauria found between Andesaurus and more highly derived genera.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, Andesaurus que es muy basal muestra vértebras caudales anfipáticas continuas, aplanadas en ambos extremos. Probablemente Epachthosaurus fue un Titanosauria basal, que se encuentra entre Andesaurus y los géneros más altamente derivados.

facts.statement: Fossils of Epachthosaurus come from the Bajo Barreal Formation in central Patagonia, Chubut Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los restos provienen de la Formación Bajo Barreal de la Provincia del Chubut, Patagonia central, Argentina.

facts.statement: Epachthosaurus is classified within the family Andesauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Andesauridae

facts.statement: The Bajo Barreal Formation dates to the latest Cenomanian and earliest Turonian of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: La Formación Bajo Barreal se remonta a los últimos años de Cenomaniano y primeros del Turoniano del Cretácico.

facts.statement: Epachthosaurus shared its environment with basal Chelidae turtles like Bonapartemys and Prochelidella, the abelisaurid Xenotarsosaurus, and an unidentified carnotaurine.
facts.quote: Otra fauna de la formación incluye la tortugas Chelidae basal Bonapartemys y Prochelidella, el abelisauroide Xenotarsosaurus y un carnotaurino no identificado.

facts.statement: Contemporaries of Epachthosaurus included the sauropod Sarmientosaurus, the ornithopod Notohypsilophodon, and the theropods Drusilasaura, Campylodoniscus, and Aniksosaurus.
facts.quote: Otros géneros que vivieron junto a Epachthosaurus son Sarmientosaurus , Notohypsilophodon, Drusilasaura , Campylodoniscus y Aniksosaurus.

facts.statement: Epachthosaurus belongs to the Lithostrotia clade.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lithostrotia

facts.statement: Epachthosaurus is classified within the Saurischia class.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The genus Epachthosaurus was named by Powell in 1990.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Epachthosaurus (genus), Powell 1990

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Epachthosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3
